mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day ahead returns in the same period are not statistically different from the prior 60-day average (p > 0.1), or the 60-day forward return is positive despite the rate increase.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 0.3% for two consecutive months, the market anticipates a pre-emptive rate cut by the Federal Reserve, which boosts equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat, and 10-day realized volatility of SPX is lower than the 30-day average prior to the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS (labor market activity) accompanied by a decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests a tight labor market, which elevates corporate earnings expectations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE decreases by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative, or the correlation between PAYEMS and UNRATE is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in GDPC1 (real private consumption) of at least 2% for two consecutive months indicates weakening demand, which compresses future earnings growth and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by >=2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from the prior 30-day average (p > 0.1), or GDPC1 recovers in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) falls by more than 5% in a month, it signals supply-side weakness that reduces growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >5% in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive, or the 10-day average realized volatility of SPX is lower than the 30-day average prior to the drop.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in FEDFUNDS for three consecutive months, despite no increase in CPIAUCSL inflation, creates expectations of persistent rate stability and supports higher equity valuations, yielding positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases for 3 consecutive months while CPIAUCSL remains flat or increases <0.1% over the same period
regime_hint: neutral to slightly restrictive monetary policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative, and the 5-day realized volatility of SPX is higher than the 30-day average.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months while HOUST (retail sales) increases by 5% or more, it indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer confidence and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for two consecutive months and HOUST increases by >5% in the same period
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.1), or the correlation between UNRATE and HOUST is not significant.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a supply-side expansion characterized by two consecutive months of double-digit growth in INDPRO and a decline in RSAFS (retail sales) suggests the economy is entering a cycle of excess capacity, which suppresses growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO grows by >10% for two consecutive months while RSAFS decreases by >5% in the same months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive, or the 20-day average of SPX daily beta against the S&P 500 is above 1.0 indicating excess sensitivity.
